summary:
Kaduna State stands under Nigeria's national framework, and its own criminal law adds two layers that a visitor has to read together. The UK Home Office country policy and information note on sexual orientation and gender identity (June 2025) records that Kaduna separately adopted its own secular Penal Code in 2017, whose Section 259 punishes 'unnatural offences' (sodomy, lesbianism and bestiality) with up to 21 years' imprisonment and a fine, a ceiling above the federal 14-year maximum.

Running in parallel, the Kaduna Sharia Penal Code Law 2002 (Law No. 4 of 2002) applies to Muslims. It was signed into law and came into operation on 21 June 2002, published in Kaduna State Gazette No. 17 Vol. 36 of 4 July 2002, and bound with the Sharia Criminal Procedure Code. Human Rights Watch (2004) traces the wave of adoption back to Zamfara's Sharia Establishment Law of 27 October 1999, in force 27 January 2000, after which twelve northern states had adopted some form of Sharia into their criminal legislation by 2002; those twelve remain the only states where Sharia courts hold jurisdiction to try criminal cases, Kaduna among them.

The Home Office's June 2025 note carries Kaduna's own row in its twelve-state Sharia penalties table (section 8.4.3, ILGA-derived): death by stoning as the maximum for liwat (sodomy), and same-sex acts between women punishable 'at the discretion of the qadi (Sharia court judge)'. Ostien's annotated volume of Kaduna's enacted text records that Kaduna is one of only three states whose statute states without qualification that 'Whoever commits the offence of sodomy shall be punished with stoning to death (rajm)', with no unmarried/married graduation, while the lesbianism offence is left to ta'azir, discretionary punishment. A trans visitor read as Muslim therefore faces a capital ceiling on men's same-sex acts under Kaduna's own promulgated code, alongside the 21-year secular ceiling that applies regardless of faith.
tangentialFactors:
Kaduna's two-layer structure is harsher than the federal baseline on both tracks: the state's secular Section 259 ceiling of 21 years exceeds the federal 14-year maximum, and its Sharia layer carries the twelve-state bloc's capital maximum for sodomy, stated in the enacted text without the unmarried/married distinction that appears in two of the other three states with the same wording.

The Home Office table derives from ILGA's documentation, and the qadi-discretion formulation for same-sex acts between women means the outcome for a woman or a trans woman read as a woman is set by an individual judge rather than by a fixed tariff.
localsOnly:
For Kaduna residents, the practical exposure combines the 2017 secular Penal Code and, for Muslims, the 2002 Sharia Penal Code, with the Sharia courts holding criminal jurisdiction in this state. The secular statute alone reaches 21 years' imprisonment plus a fine for 'unnatural offences'.

The Sharia layer's stoning-to-death provision for sodomy is enacted text, not a maximum that requires a further legislative step, and the lesbianism provision is discretionary with the qadi.
outOfScopeNotes:
The inventory does not document any Kaduna-specific enforcement incident, arrest, prosecution or killing under either statute; the enforcement record cited in the national framework concerns other states. Whether the 21-year secular ceiling or the Sharia capital provision has been applied in any recent Kaduna case is unresolved on these sources.

How the two layers interact for a non-Muslim charged under Section 259, and whether the Sharia layer's jurisdiction over Muslims is limited by offence or by the accused's stated faith, is not sourced here.
